         SWG BRIGGS I, L.P.’S RESPONSE TO ONCOR AND LCRA TSC’S LIST OF

           On March 26, 2026, Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) and LCRA

Transmission Services Corporation (“LCRA TSC,” and, together with Oncor, “Applicants”) filed

a joint application to amend their certificates of convenience and necessity for the Bell County

East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765 kilovolt (“kV”) transmission line project in Bell, Burnet,

Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba,

Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson Counties, Texas.

           On March 30, 2026, the Public Utility Commission of Texas referred this docket to the

State Office of Administrative Hearings (“SOAH”). On March 31, 2026, the SOAH Administrative

Law Judges (“ALJs”) issued SOAH Order No. 1, which established April 27, 2026 as the deadline

to intervene. 1

           On April 20, 2026, the SOAH ALJs issued SOAH Order No. 6, which, among other things,

(1) established May 13, 2026, as the deadline for intervenors to file testimony or a statement of


1

 position; (2) ordered that, if an intervenor fails to timely file direct testimony or a statement of

position, the ALJs “will dismiss them as a party [...] [and] will be prohibited from participating in

the hearing on the merits and briefing;” 2 and (3) instructed Applicants to file by May 15, 2026, a

list of intervenors who did not file direct testimony or a statement of position. 3

           On May 15, 2026, Applicants filed a list of intervenors who allegedly did not file direct

testimony or a statement of position. However, the list improperly included SWG Briggs I, L.P.

                                               I.      ARGUMENT

           SWG Briggs I, L.P. timely filed its Request to Intervene on April 27, 2026, in compliance

with SOAH Order No. 1. See Item No. 3043. On the same date, the undersigned counsel filed a

Notice of Appearance on behalf of SWG Briggs I, L.P. See Item No. 3167.

           Consistent with SOAH Order No. 6, SWG Briggs I, L.P. timely filed its direct testimony

in this proceeding on May 13, 2026. See Item No. 3976. A true and correct copy of the Direct

Testimony of Amy G. Thomason on behalf of SWG Briggs I, L.P. is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

           Accordingly, SWG Briggs I, L.P. fully complied with all applicable deadlines and

requirements set forth in the ALJs’ orders. Its inclusion on Applicants’ list of non-compliant

intervenors is erroneous and without basis. SWG Briggs I, L.P. should therefore not be subject to

dismissal and must be permitted to continue participating fully in this proceeding.

                                         II.        RELIEF REQUESTED

           SWG Briggs I, L.P. respectfully requests that the ALJs:

      1. Confirm that SWG Briggs I, L.P. timely filed its direct testimony in compliance with SOAH

           Order No. 6;

                                    I.      INTRODUCTION

Q.    Please state your name and address.

A.    My name is Dr. Amy G. Thomason. My address is 8408 Bear Creek Drive, Austin, Texas
      78737.
Q.    Please state your background.

A.    I am a licensed veterinarian in the State of Texas and have been licensed since 2007.

Q.    Who are you testifying on behalf of?

A.    I am testifying on behalf of SWG Briggs I, L.P.

Q.    Has SWG Briggs I, L.P intervened in this proceeding (PUC Dkt. No. 59475)?

A.    Yes. SWG Briggs I, L.P filed a Motion to Intervene in PUC Dkt. No. 59475 on April 27,
      2026 (Item 3043).

Q.    How are you connected with SWG Briggs I, L.P.?

A.    I am the Manager-Member of SWG Briggs, LLC, which is the General Partner of SWG
      Briggs I, L.P. I have authority to testify on behalf of SWG Briggs I, L.P.

Q.    Does SWG Briggs I, L.P own property that will potentially be affected by the proposed
      transmission line project?

A.    Yes. SWGBriggs I, L.P. owns property in Burnet County, including Tracts 5128,5132, and
      5133 (as identified in the application), all of which will be crossed by proposed Link G9.
      See Exhibit A, Map of G9 Link and Highlighted Tracts 5128, 5132, and 5133 (the
      "Properties").

      Tract 5128 is identified as Property ID 58551 in the Burnet County Appraisal District
      (Legal Description: ABS A1211 JOHN B. BAKER, 1.0 ACRES).

      Tract 5132 is identified as Property ID 58552 in the Burnet County Appraisal District
      (Legal Description: ABS A1211 JOHN B. BAKER, TRACT AND TCRR ABST 1357,
      221.708 ACRES).

      Tract 5133 is identified as Property ID 59158 in the Burnet County Appraisal District
      (Legal Description: ABS A1357 T.C.R.R.CO., TRACT ABSTS 187 M 369,
      370,806,1001,1164,1184,1588,121,1372.405 ACRES).

      Exhibit B contains deeds establishing SWG Briggs I, L.P.'s ownership of these tracts.




DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                            3
 Q.    What is the purpose of your testimony?

A.    The purpose of my testimony is to provide evidence supporting the rejection or
      modification of routes incorporating Link G9. These routes directly impact SWG Briggs I,
      L.P.'s Properties (my family's ranch). I also address the severe and irreparable harm that a
      765 kV transmission line would cause to property values, health, operations, groundwater
      resources, heritage land, and the Northeast Burnet County Water District 1.

                                   II.    PROJECT IMPACT

Q.    What routes impact SWG Briggs I, L.P's properties?

A.    Link G9, as utilized in Routes 266,524,535,543,546,547,548,557,668,729,900, and
      905 for the Bell County East-Big Hill 765 kV transmission line project. These routes would
      cross the Properties directly. According to the application, the proposed right-of-way
      ("ROW") is approximately 200 feet wide, with structures up to 198 feet tall and
      approximately 141 feet in width. These structures and the ROW would occupy and bisect
      the Properties.

Q.    Which routes do you oppose?

A.    I oppose Routes 266,524,535,543,546,547,548,557,668,729,900, and 905 as they all
      include Link G9. These routes bisect the Properties and impact the Northeast Burnet
      County Water District 1.

      I urge the Commission to reject the proposed Routes 266,524,535,543,546,547,548,
      557,668,729,900, and 905, as well as Link G9 itself. The proposed routing fails to
      adequately minimize impacts to landowners, agricultural operations, and community
      values, as required under the Commission's routing criteria, including the policy of prudent
      avoidance. Reasonable alternative routes exist that would better utilize compatible
      corridors and maintain greater separation from occupied structures and active agricultural
      operations.

Q.    Which routes do you support?

A.    I support routes that follow or parallel existing infrastructure corridors; maintain a
      minimum 1,500-foot distance from habitable structures; avoid the Northeast Burnet
      County Water District 1 and environmentally sensitive areas; and minimize impacts to
      agricultural operations and heritage lands.

Q.    Have you testified before at the Public Utility Commission of Texas?

A.    No.

Q.    Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision and guidance?




DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                             4
 A.    Yes.

                            III.    DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY

Q.    Could you please provide a brief description of the Properties?

A.    Our family ranch comprises approximately 1,886 acres of land located in Burnet County
      and includes Tracts 5128, 5132, and 5133, as identified in the application materials. The
      Properties have been owned and operated by our family since the late 1990s and are
      actively used for agricultural operations, including cattle ranching and hay production. The
      ranch currently supports approximately 60 head of cattle and includes active hay farming
      operations.

Q.    Please give a brief history of the property and your association with it.

A.    The Properties have been in our family's ownership since the late 1990s. The ranch has
      served as an important long-term family agricultural and rural residential property in
      Burnet County for decades. The land represents not only a substantial financial investment,
      but also an irreplaceable family legacy tied to ranching, land stewardship, and preservation
      of the rural character of the area.

Q.    Please describe how the Properties are used today and how this transmission line may
      affect that use.

A.    The Properties support white-tailed deer, migratory birds, and other native wildlife. The
      proposed Link G9, if constructed as proposed, would permanently damage the Properties
      in several ways, including rendering portions of the land unsuitable for their current uses
      due to the presence of transmission towers, conductors, and associated easements.

      Additionally, portions of the Properties lie within the Northeast Burnet County Water
      District 1 (see Exhibit C , MUD Map ), which was created on June 7 , 2019 , through an act
      ofthe Texas Legislature (see Exhibit D, H.B. 4669). The proposed Link G9 could adversely
      affect the Water District by interfering with exi sting and planned water infrastructure,
      including wells, pipelines, and related facilities; restricting the placement and expansion of
      such infrastructure due to transmission easements and setback requirements; and increasing
      the risk of erosion, sedimentation, or other environmental impacts that could affect water
      quality within the Water District. These impacts may impair the Water District's ability to
      plan, develop, and operate water service facilities necessary to serve current and future
      users.

Q.    How would the proposed transmission line affect your agricultural operations?

A.    The proposed transmission line would materially interfere with our ongoing agricultural
      operations. The Properties are actively used for cattle ranching and hay production,
      including maintaining approximately 60 head of cattle. The proposed ROW and
      transmission structures would fragment pasture areas, interfere with cattle movement and



DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                               5
       grazing patterns, reduce usable acreage for hay production, and create operational
      complications for ranch equipment and agricultural management activities.

      The permanent easement corridor would also impair future agricultural flexibility and
      diminish the long-term viability and value of the ranch as an agricultural property. These
      impacts would not be temporary; they would remain for the life of the transmission
      facilities.

Q.    What do you think the financial risks will be to SWG Briggs I, L.P.?

A.    The financial risks to my family are severe and likely permanent. The Properties are not
      speculative investment land. They are actively operated agricultural and rural residential
      properties supporting cattle ranching, hay production, and ongoing family use. The
      Properties represent a significant family asset. The placement of a 765 kV transmission
      line, with towers up to 198 feet tall, would substantially interfere with those plans by
      limiting suitable home sites, imposing setback and safety constraints, and placing large-
      scale transmission infrastructure in close proximity to any future residence. As a result, the
      line would materially diminish our ability to use and enjoy the property for its intended
      residential purpose. In addition, the presence of a 765 kV line-the highest voltage class
      in common use-near a home would significantly reduce the desirability and market value
      of the property.

Q.    What are the risks of devaluation of your property?

A.    As noted, the proj ect would significantly devalue the Properties. The proposed Link G9,
      once established as a permanent 200-foot ROW, would adversely affect the marketability
      and appraised value of land that has been held in our family since the late 1990s. Land
      within or adjacent to a transmission ROW loses value because: (1) tower footprints and
      ROW corridors remove productive acreage from cultivation and grazing; (2) prospective
      buyers discount properties burdened by transmission easements; and (3) the visual and
      audible presence of transmission lines diminishes the rural character and aesthetic value
      that drive land prices in Burnet County. The application documents acknowledge that the
      proj ect will create permanent aesthetic impacts, with structures and wires remaining visible
      indefinitely.

Q.    What do you see as safety risks?

A.    The safety risks of a 765 kV transmission line bisecting the Properties are substantial.
      Burnet County experiences severe weather events, including high winds and occasional
      tornadoes. A tower collapse or conductor failure under such conditions could be
      catastrophic. Additionally, there is a risk of fire, particularly in an area that has experienced
      significant wildfire events in the past.

Q.    Do you have concerns regarding potential health effects associated with locating a 765
      kV transmission line through the Properties?




DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                                  6
 A.    Yes. I am concerned about noise, stress, visual impacts, fire risk, and the psychological
      burden associated with anyone living immediately adjacent to a 765 kV transmission
      corridor.

Q.    What do you think will be the environmental impacts and risks?

A.    The environmental impacts to the Properties appear to be significant. As acknowledged in
      the application, soil erosion presents a substantial risk during and after ROW clearing. The
      clearing and grading of a wide transmission corridor would expose soils to erosion by wind
      and water, potentially causing long-term degradation of the land.

      In addition, the removal of native vegetation within the ROW would result in the loss of
      wildlife habitat, including habitat used by white-tailed deer, migratory birds, and other
      native species. This fragmentation of habitat may disrupt movement patterns, reduce cover,
      and diminish the ecological value of the Properties.

      Construction activities also pose risks of sediment runoffinto nearby drainage areas, which
      could affect surface water quality, particularly during heavy rainfall events. Disturbance of
      soils and vegetation may further increase the potential for invasive species to establish
      within the corridor, leading to long-term changes in the native plant community.

      The installation and long-term presence of large transmission structures may also affect
      avian species through collision risk and habitat disruption. Additionally, ongoing
      maintenance activities, including vegetation management within the ROW, would result in
      continued disturbance and limit the natural regrowth of native vegetation.

      Taken together, these impacts could result in lasting environmental degradation of the
      Properties, affecting soil stability, vegetation, wildlife habitat, and overall ecological
      function.

Q.    How would the proposed transmission lines affect your enjoyment of the Properties?

A.    The proposed Link G9 would devastate our family's enjoyment ofthe Properties. The land,
      which has been in our family since the late 1990s, is located in rural Burnet County, an
      area we value for its natural beauty, clear skies, and open views. The installation of steel
      towers (up to 198 feet tall) on or near the Properties would permanently eliminate those
      qualities. The visual impact would be immediate and overwhelming. In addition, the
      audible effects producing persistent buzzing and crackling sounds would intrude at all
      hours. These impacts would permanently impair our ability to use and enjoy the Properties
      for living, recreation, and family gatherings.

Q.    Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use on
      your land?

A.    Yes. The Properties are intended for future generations of our family to enjoy. We have
      long-term plans to maintain the land as rural property, consistent with its history since the



DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                              7
       late 1990s. The presence of a 765 kV transmission line would significantly reduce the value
      of the land and eliminate its viability for potential residential use. Land values in this area
      are closely tied to its rural character, which the proposed Link G9 would permanently
      compromise.

Q.    How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your area?

A.    Burnet County's rural western areas retain the agricultural heritage and open-land character
      that define the community's values. Our family has been part of this community since the
      late 1990s, contributing to its ranching and the stewardship of its natural resources. The
      construction of a 765 kV transmission line through the Properties would fragment the
      landscape, reduce property values for all landowners, and alter the visual and economic
      character ofthe community. This is not an isolated concern, but one that affects the broader
      community.

Q.    How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?

A.    The aesthetic impact of the proposed Link G9 would be substantial and permanent. The
      application acknowledges that aesthetic impacts occur when new structures alter the visual
      character of the environment. For the Properties, this would result in a complete loss of the
      natural scenic character. Tower lighting would introduce ongoing light pollution into what
      is currently a dark rural setting. No amount of landscaping or vegetation could adequately
      screen a 198-foot steel lattice tower from view.

      The visual intrusion would be especially severe because the transmission line would be
      located in close proximity to residence and ranch improvements, all of which currently
      enjoy unobstructed rural views and dark-sky conditions characteristic of Burnet County.
      The industrial scale of a 765 kV line is fundamentally incompatible with the existing rural
      and agricultural character of the Properties.

                       IV.     PROJECT NEED AND ALTERNATIVES

Q.    Do you have concerns regarding the stated need for this project and how it is
      designed?

A.    Yes. Because the Properties may be affected by the proposed project, I have concerns about
      whether this transmission line is the best approach and whether other options have been
      fully considered.

      Like many other Texans, I remember the impacts of Winter Storm Uri in February 2021
      and the widespread outages that affected many parts of Texas, including Central Texas. In
      light of those events, I question why additional transmission capacity is being directed
      away from Central Texas when there have already been concerns about reliability and
      infrastructure needs in this region.




DIRECT TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON
       I also understand that the Permian Basin is an area with substantial oil and gas activity and
      significant natural gas production. It seems reasonable to ask whether additional power
      generation closer to where the demand exists could reduce the need for large transmission
      lines crossing private property and rural land.

      In general, I believe it is important for all reasonable alternatives to be considered before
      placing infrastructure of this size and scale across private property.

Q.    Why are these concerns important in this proceeding?

A.    These concerns are important to me because this project would permanently affect private
      landowners, including agricultural and rural properties like ours. A 765 kV transmission
      line is a major piece of infrastructure with long-term impacts on the use, appearance, and
      value ofproperty.

      Because of those impacts, I believe projects like this should only be approved when
      absolutely necessary and when reasonable alternatives have been carefully evaluated. As a
      landowner, I want to ensure that the impacts to private property are minimized wherever
      possible.

Q.    How does this relate to your opposition to Link G9 and the proposed routes?

A.    My concerns about the proj ect generally are part of the reason I oppose Link G9 and the
      proposed routes affecting the Properties and surrounding community. From my
      perspective, if there are other reasonable ways to address future electric demand or reduce
      the need for long-distance transmission, those options should be considered before routing
      a transmission line of this magnitude across private land.

      Even if additional infrastructure is ultimately needed, I believe routing decisions should
      prioritize minimizing impacts to homes, agricultural operations, and existing land uses,
      including by using existing utility corridors whenever feasible.

Q:    Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?

A.    At this time, I respectfully request that the Commission fully consider the long-term
      impacts to our family, the Properties, and the surrounding community when evaluating the
      proposed proj ect.

Q.    Does this conclude your testimony?

A.    Yes, at present it does, but I reserve the right to amend or supplement my testimony.
